statutes.act: A Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: The appellant felt aggrieved by an order dated 2nd July, 2001 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Sihora, in sessions trial No.469 of 1998 whereby the appellant has been charge-sheeted for an offence under Section 306 of the Indian Penal Code, filed a petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the charge before the High Court without any result, hence the appeal.
The marriage between the sister of the appellant and the deceased took place in 1993.
Immediately after marriage she was subjected to continuous ill-treatment by the deceased and the family members forcing her to live separately along with her husband and children for about a year.
Thereafter, she went to her parents' house and started living with her brother the appellant herein.
The appellant advised the deceased to take his sister back to her matrimonial house and treat her properly.

On 25th July, 1998 (crucial date), it is stated that the appellant visited the place of the parents of the deceased and pleaded with them that his sister should be rehabilitated in the matrimonial home and should not be physically ill-treated or harassed.
The deceased went to the house of the parents of the appellant followed by a quarrel between them.
On 27th July, 1998, the deceased was found hanging with a rope by neck on the raft of his house and he was found dead.
issues: Whether the charge-sheeted offence under Section 306 I.P.C. is sustainable merely on the allegation of harassment to the deceased?
Whether the alleged abusive words uttered by the appellant on 25th July, 1998 constitute the ingredient of 'instigation'?
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution story that the suicide by the deceased is the direct result of the quarrel that had taken place on 25th July, 1998 wherein it is alleged that the appellant had used abusive language and had reportedly told the deceased 'to go and die' is erroneous.

The courts below have relied on a statement of Shashi Bhushan, brother of the deceased, made under Section 161 Cr.P.C. when reportedly the deceased, after coming back from the house of the appellant, told him that the appellant had humiliated him and abused him with filthy words.
Even if we accept the prosecution story that the appellant did tell the deceased 'to go and die', that itself does not constitute the ingredient of 'instigation'.
respondent_arguments: The charge-sheeted offence under Section 306 I.P.C. is sustainable merely on the allegation of harassment to the deceased.
The alleged abusive words uttered by the appellant on 25th July, 1998 constitute the ingredient of 'instigation' and the presence of mens rea is not necessary for instigation.
court_reasoning: Mere words uttered by the accused to the deceased 'to go and die' were not even prima facie enough to instigate the deceased to commit suicide.
A word uttered in a fit of anger or emotion without intending the consequences to actually follow cannot be said to be instigation.
The conscience of the court should not be satisfied for basing a finding that the accused charged for abetting the offence of suicide should be found guilty.
holding: The charge-sheeted offence under Section 306 I.P.C. is not sustainable merely on the allegation of harassment to the deceased.
The alleged abusive words uttered by the appellant on 25th July, 1998 do not constitute the ingredient of 'instigation'.
